deviations.qemu_behavior: Recalled from QEMU's hw/audio/intel-hda.c and hw/audio/hda-codec.c, not re-read for this entry. Medium confidence: QEMU's virtual Intel HDA moves output-stream DMA from its hda-duplex/hda-output codec, which by default (the use-timer property) runs a timer on QEMU's virtual clock that keeps the bytes taken from guest memory in step with the stream rate and the audio backend's consumption. Each transfer walks the BDL, updates LPIB and an enabled DMA position buffer, sets BCIS on a completed entry flagged IOC and updates the controller interrupt, through MSI when the guest enabled it, else INTx. The pace therefore depends neither on vCPU exits nor on a host thread of the VMM.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: BridgeVM's HDA controller (crates/bridgevm-hvf/src/hda) advances playback DMA by the host time elapsed since the previous poll of the controller, at most 100 ms per poll (longer gaps drop the excess). A poll runs in every vCPU drain, before CPU0 runs and after any vCPU's MMIO exit, and, from this change, in a host service tick every 5 ms while SD0CTL.RUN is set (examples/hvf_gic_boot_probe/hda_service_tick.rs). The tick is deadline-paced at user-interactive QoS, takes the platform lock only with try_lock and skips a tick a vCPU or a reset holds, sends the MSI it takes after releasing the lock, never forces a vCPU exit, and is off under BRIDGEVM_USERSPACE_GIC, where exits alone poll as before. A completed IOC entry sets BCIS, and an MSI is sent only on a rising edge of the controller's interrupt level, so entries completed within one poll share one MSI. The function is MSI-only: it advertises no INTx pin. LPIB and an enabled position buffer advance in poll-sized steps.
deviations.impact: The guest sees DMA progress and IOC interrupts at the polls' granularity rather than QEMU's timer cadence. Before this change that granularity was the guest's own exit pattern: T17 r92 recorded poll gaps up to 216 ms against Windows' 20 ms cyclic buffer, so audio the guest had not rewritten was played again, 116 ms was dropped, and 372 MSIs covered 568 IOCs. With the tick the expected gap is at most 5 ms plus the host's wake latency while the stream runs, and longer only while a vCPU holds the platform lock, when that vCPU's drain polls instead. Only deterministic tests at this change support that expectation; no live run has measured the guest-visible pacing, and the QEMU description is recalled, not re-read.
